conditions: Real observation x; reference population has finite mean and strictly positive finite standard deviation. Normality is not required for standardization; a standardized nonnormal variable is not necessarily normally distributed.

evidence: Subtract the population mean from X and divide by its positive finite standard deviation. Linearity of expectation gives mean zero, and the variance scaling law gives variance one. For a specified observed x the quotient measures signed distance from mu in units of sigma. This does not make a nonnormal distribution normal.
